html:
Pescado, Spanish for "fish", is the name the map gives a territory in northern Chihuahua, west of the Rio Grande. Standard sources say little about a people by this name; it may come from a Spanish colonial label for a local band.

The peoples of this desert and river country in the 1500s and 1600s included the Suma, the Janos, the Jumanos and the Concho. They lived by hunting, gathering mesquite and agave, and some farming along the rivers. Spanish missions, mines and slave raids from the late 1500s, under the Viceroyalty of New Spain, broke up these groups, and Apache raids later finished the process.
